name: Optimize Gleam rewrite for speed/stability while preserving parity

description: Baseline in-process parity+benchmark harness (quality+form workloads) after initial Gleam port

asi.hypothesis: Establish a trustworthy baseline metric combining speed ratio and parity checks before optimization.

description: Add fast unique-assignment DP path for equal team/task sizes in Gleam scoring to remove factorial blowup in quality workloads

asi.hypothesis: Replacing exhaustive equal-partition assignment with memoized bitmask DP will drastically reduce quality benchmark runtime without changing outputs.
asi.observations: combined_ratio improved 14.76 -> 3.67; quality_ratio dropped 67.9 -> 4.29 while parity checks still passed.
asi.next_action_hint: Focus next on formation speed for larger workloads (second form workload still ~8.5x python).

description: Memoize formation subproblems by remaining tasks+people signatures to reduce repeated exact-search work

asi.hypothesis: Caching explore_tasks results for repeated remaining-person/task states will improve formation performance and stability.
asi.observations: combined_ratio improved 3.67 -> 3.27 and form_ratio improved 3.14 -> 2.37; medium workload form ratio dropped from ~8.5x to ~5.4x.
asi.next_action_hint: Reduce quality ratio next by avoiding repeated JSON decode overhead in bench path and optimizing decode/score hot paths without changing semantics.

description: No-code-change rerun to sample benchmark noise; apparent improvement likely variance (form ratio stdev very high).

asi.hypothesis: Re-running the current best commit without code changes will estimate noise before attempting further optimizations.
asi.rollback_reason: Discarded because this was a pure rerun with no implementation change and high variance (stability_cv≈0.99), so lower metric is not attributable to a real optimization.
asi.next_action_hint: Reduce benchmark noise (more iterations or robust median) and then optimize hot paths in form scoring/search.
asi.observations: form workload run2 remained much slower than run1, indicating unstable timings in current harness.

description: Remove deterministic sorting during Gleam JSON/result serialization and assigned-people conversion to cut repeated per-call overhead in quality/form paths.

asi.hypothesis: Dropping redundant list.sort calls on dict-derived structures will reduce overhead in hot output/formation conversion paths without changing semantic JSON objects.
asi.observations: combined_ratio improved versus previous kept run (3.27 -> 3.17) and quality_ratio dropped to 4.24; form timings remain noisy with high CV.
asi.next_action_hint: Target core scoring hot path next (coverage + assignment DP/memo lookups) where quality ratio is still >4x.

description: Use set-based duplicate detection and single-pass member preference validation in request model checks.

asi.hypothesis: Replacing dict-count duplicate checks with set-based scans and combining duplicate/unknown preference validation into one pass should lower decode/validation overhead.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary metric regressed slightly (3.1738 -> 3.1927) and no stability improvement; change does not show measurable benchmark win.
asi.next_action_hint: Focus on scoring hot path (unique assignment DP and repeated coverage calculations) rather than validation overhead.
asi.observations: quality_ratio and form_ratio both moved slightly worse; benchmark variance remains high on second form workload.

description: Encode unique-assignment DP keys as Ints (score/memo) instead of tuple keys to reduce dict lookup/allocation overhead in scoring hot path.

asi.hypothesis: Replacing tuple dict keys with compact Int keys in the unique assignment DP will reduce hashing/allocation overhead and speed quality scoring.
asi.observations: quality_ratio improved materially (4.24 -> 3.99) and combined_ratio improved to 3.0649 while maintaining parity checks.
asi.next_action_hint: Continue reducing quality hot-path cost by specializing compat coverage calculation and minimizing repeated safe_log/dict lookups inside DP.

description: Precompute log-scores in unique assignment matrix and derive geometric mean directly from DP best-state log objective.

asi.hypothesis: Avoiding repeated safe_log calls and post-DP score reconstruction should reduce unique assignment overhead.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary metric regressed versus current best (3.0649 -> 3.0937); optimization did not produce measurable speedup.
asi.next_action_hint: Try compat-specific coverage specialization and reducing formation benchmark variance before further DP tuning.
asi.observations: quality_ratio stayed near 4.0 and form_ratio remained noise-dominated, suggesting this change was neutral/slightly negative in practice.

description: Specialize coverage_for_person_and_task_skill by mode to streamline compat path and hoist Paper required-level computation.

asi.hypothesis: Splitting compat/paper branches at function entry would remove per-skill mode checks and lower coverage-call overhead.
asi.rollback_reason: Combined metric regressed materially (3.0649 -> 3.1975), with worse quality and form ratios.
asi.next_action_hint: Investigate formation-specific hotspots (candidate loop allocations and repeated preference/set construction) instead of micro-optimizing coverage branch structure.
asi.observations: Despite lower control-flow branching in compat path, runtime worsened, likely due extra function-call/branch costs in generated JS.

description: Hoist per-task preference lookup/default resolution out of candidate loop in formation search to avoid repeated recomputation for every candidate team.

asi.hypothesis: Task preference maps/defaults are invariant per task, so computing them once per explore_tasks level should reduce formation-search overhead.
asi.observations: combined_ratio improved strongly (3.0649 -> 2.8017), driven by form_ratio drop (2.35 -> 1.95) while quality ratio stayed roughly flat.
asi.next_action_hint: Further trim candidate-loop allocations (teammate-id sets/social preference checks/assigned-person conversion) and target remaining quality-ratio gap.

description: Defer assigned-people list conversion during formation search by storing assignment dicts in SearchOutcome and materializing TeamResult only for final output.

asi.hypothesis: Avoiding per-candidate assigned_people conversion should reduce allocation overhead in formation recursion.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary metric was slightly worse than current best (2.8017 -> 2.8063), so no clear improvement to keep.
asi.next_action_hint: Target quality hot path next (decode/validation and assignment matrix work), and consider benchmark-noise reduction for form runs.
asi.observations: form_ratio stayed close to best (~1.94) but quality_ratio drifted higher (~4.06), leaving combined result marginally worse.

description: Store quality weights as typed Weights record (not Dict) and encode fixed weight fields directly to cut per-call dict construction/iteration overhead.

asi.hypothesis: Eliminating dict materialization/traversal for the 4 weight values will reduce serialization and scoring overhead.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary metric regressed (2.8017 -> 3.0440) despite better quality_ratio; form_ratio worsened enough to hurt combined objective.
asi.next_action_hint: If revisiting, pair this quality-focused optimization with formation-loop improvements and confirm on multiple runs due form noise.
asi.observations: quality_ratio improved to 3.93, but form_ratio jumped to 2.36 in this run.

description: Skip per-candidate teammate-set/social-preference scans when current people pool has no non-self social preferences.

asi.hypothesis: Most benchmark people only have self-preferences, so bypassing candidate-level social-preference detection should speed formation search.
asi.rollback_reason: Combined metric regressed heavily (2.8017 -> 3.1383) due worse form ratio, so change is not viable for primary objective.
asi.next_action_hint: Focus on reducing allocations in combination/removal paths or quality-side improvements that do not inflate form runtime.
asi.observations: quality_ratio dropped to 3.79 in this run, but form_ratio increased to 2.60 and dominated the combined score.

description: No-code-change rerun to sample current benchmark variance around latest kept commit.

asi.hypothesis: Re-running the unchanged best commit will quantify measurement noise before further tuning.
asi.rollback_reason: Discarded because this run includes no implementation change and metric drifted upward; used only for variance sampling.
asi.next_action_hint: Stabilize benchmark (more repetitions/robust aggregation) or require repeated confirmation for tiny deltas before keeping.
asi.observations: combined_ratio moved from 2.80 to 2.94 with unchanged code; both quality and form components show large run-to-run spread.

description: Pre-resolve formation weights once per request and pass fixed alpha/beta/gamma/delta to candidate scoring to avoid repeated weight resolution.

asi.hypothesis: Hoisting resolve_weights out of the candidate loop should cut repeated preset/normalization overhead in form search.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary metric regressed (2.8017 -> 3.0259), so this refactor does not improve the combined objective.
asi.next_action_hint: Investigate quality-path bottlenecks directly or pursue form optimizations with larger impact on second workload.
asi.observations: form_ratio improved slightly vs some recent runs but quality_ratio worsened substantially in this run, leading to net regression.

description: Add scoring API overrides to skip social-score computation for compat teams without explicit social preferences, and use it in formation candidate scoring.

asi.hypothesis: By overriding social_score=0.0 in compat no-social cases, formation can avoid expensive team_social_score work while preserving adjusted quality semantics.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary metric regressed (2.8017 -> 2.9597), so the override path did not improve the combined benchmark.
asi.next_action_hint: Revisit quality-path optimizations (decode/encode overhead) and keep form changes narrowly focused on second workload hotspots.
asi.observations: form_ratio around 2.03 was not enough to offset quality_ratio increase to 4.31; net combined score worsened.

description: Replace remove_people set-build/filter path with direct small-list membership scans to reduce per-candidate allocation overhead.

asi.hypothesis: For tiny candidate team sizes, linear membership checks should outperform constructing a set every time in remove_people.
asi.rollback_reason: Combined metric regressed (2.8017 -> 3.1083), so the change did not improve the primary objective.
asi.next_action_hint: Try optimizations that directly reduce quality benchmark overhead (parse/encode/scoring) since form-side micro changes are not producing wins.
asi.observations: form ratio did not improve enough and quality ratio fluctuated higher in this run.

description: Remove sorting from formation memo people signature to avoid per-state list.sort during recursive cache-key generation.

asi.hypothesis: people_signature sorting is redundant because remaining people preserve canonical order, so removing sort should reduce memo-key overhead.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary metric regressed (2.8017 -> 3.0825); expected form speedup did not materialize in combined benchmark.
asi.next_action_hint: Try stronger form optimizations (non-string memo keys or lighter cache-key construction) and quality-path improvements.
asi.observations: form_ratio and quality_ratio both worse in this run; change appears neutral-to-negative under current harness.

description: Refactor unique-assignment result assembly to avoid member-index/score dict reconstruction by applying assignment pairs directly.

asi.hypothesis: Skipping post-DP dict materialization for member scores and member lookups will reduce quality-path overhead in unique assignment.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary metric regressed significantly (2.8017 -> 3.1430), so refactor did not improve runtime.
asi.next_action_hint: Explore lower-level hot paths (coverage matrix construction and decode/validation) or revisit form cache-key representation.
asi.observations: quality_ratio improved only slightly while form_ratio worsened heavily in this sample; no net gain.

description: Shrink formation memo key by replacing task-signature string with remaining-task-count integer (tasks are processed as ordered suffixes).

asi.hypothesis: Using task count instead of joined task-id signatures will reduce cache-key construction overhead in recursive form search.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary metric regressed (2.8017 -> 3.0138), so this memo-key simplification did not improve combined performance.
asi.next_action_hint: Prioritize quality-path speedups with larger expected gains, and revisit form memo-key work with a more radical non-string people state representation.
asi.observations: form ratio stayed near ~2.05 but quality ratio climbed to ~4.43 in this run, giving a worse combined score.

description: Fuse TeamQualityRequest team conversion and task-preference extraction into one fold to reduce extra passes/allocations in quality path.

asi.hypothesis: Combining member->person conversion with task-preference dict building in a single traversal will reduce quality request overhead.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary metric regressed (2.8017 -> 3.0336), with worse quality ratio in this run.
asi.next_action_hint: Look for larger algorithmic wins in quality assignment/scoring rather than small pass fusion refactors.
asi.observations: form ratio remained near prior levels, but quality ratio rose to ~4.55 and dominated regression.

description: Replace dict-based social preference lookups with direct preference-list scans in team social scoring to avoid per-member map construction.

asi.hypothesis: In typical small preference lists, linear scans should be cheaper than building temporary dicts for social score computation.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary metric did not improve versus best kept result (2.8017 vs 2.8088), so this change is not retained.
asi.next_action_hint: Consider adaptive hybrid lookup (scan for tiny lists, dict for larger lists) or focus on assignment/formation hot paths with larger upside.
asi.observations: Form ratio stayed strong (~1.96) and quality ratio stayed near baseline, but combined metric remained slightly worse.

description: Single-pass personality aggregation for 3+ member teams (stddev sums, ETJ/introvert maxima, genders) to reduce repeated folds/maps in personality scoring.

asi.hypothesis: Collapsing many per-team personality passes into one fold will lower scoring overhead in both quality and formation paths.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary metric regressed (2.8017 -> 3.0071), so the fold-aggregation refactor is not a win for the benchmark objective.
asi.next_action_hint: Investigate other high-impact hotspots; this path may increase generated JS overhead despite fewer traversals.
asi.observations: quality ratio was near baseline, but form ratio worsened and variability increased (stability_cv ~1.33).

description: Optimize assign_task_skills setup by bypassing similarity-index construction in Compat mode and reusing cached task/team counts instead of repeated list.length calls.

asi.hypothesis: Skipping unnecessary similarity lookup in Compat mode plus avoiding repeated length traversals will reduce hot-path setup overhead for quality/form scoring.
asi.observations: combined_ratio improved (2.8017 -> 2.7888), with slight gains in both quality_ratio (4.02 -> 3.99) and form_ratio (1.95 -> 1.95).
asi.next_action_hint: Continue tuning scoring setup/assignment hotspots and seek a larger quality-path reduction while guarding against form variance.

description: Add fast-path weight resolution for fully specified alpha/beta/gamma/delta without normalization to skip preset/option machinery in scoring.

asi.hypothesis: When all weights are explicitly provided and normalize=false (common benchmark path), direct construction should reduce per-score overhead.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary metric regressed substantially (2.7888 -> 3.0636), driven by worse form ratio; change not beneficial for target metric.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep chasing assignment/search path wins; consider benchmarking this idea separately with repeated runs if revisited.
asi.observations: quality_ratio improved strongly (~3.80) but form_ratio degraded sharply (~2.47), causing net loss.

description: Use dict.has_key guard before memo dict.get in formation/scoring recursion to reduce Result(Error) allocations on cache misses.

asi.hypothesis: Avoiding repeated Error(Nil) creation from dict.get misses in recursive memo lookups will reduce allocation overhead.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary metric regressed sharply (2.7888 -> 3.1920), especially on form ratio; change is not beneficial.
asi.next_action_hint: Back away from extra has_key checks; they likely add lookup overhead that outweighs saved allocations.
asi.observations: form_ratio worsened to ~2.51 with this approach, indicating double-lookup cost dominated.

description: Replace remove_people list.filter closure with explicit recursive loop to reduce higher-order overhead in formation candidate expansion.

asi.hypothesis: Manual recursion for people filtering will reduce list/filter callback overhead in the form search hot path.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary metric regressed (2.7888 -> 2.9230); form improved slightly but quality ratio worsened enough to lose overall.
asi.next_action_hint: Pursue optimizations that improve quality and form together or isolate quality-only changes from form path side effects.
asi.observations: form_ratio dropped to ~1.94, but quality_ratio rose to ~4.40 and dominated combined regression.

description: Specialize unique-assignment matrix scoring for Compat mode with direct exact-skill coverage helper, bypassing generic mode/similarity coverage path.

asi.hypothesis: Compat-only direct coverage computation in unique assignment matrix build will reduce per-cell scoring overhead.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary metric regressed (2.7888 -> 2.9244); despite quality improvements, form ratio worsened significantly.
asi.next_action_hint: If revisiting, scope this specialization to quality endpoint only or pair it with a form-side optimization to offset regressions.
asi.observations: quality_ratio improved strongly (~3.83) but form_ratio rose to ~2.23 and dominated combined metric.

description: Inline best-outcome comparison in choose_best_candidate to avoid constructing candidate SearchOutcome objects when not improving current best.

asi.hypothesis: Deferring SearchOutcome allocation until objective beats current best should reduce candidate-loop allocations in formation search.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary metric regressed heavily (2.7888 -> 3.3384), so allocation deferral did not help in practice.
asi.next_action_hint: Avoid refactors that add branch complexity in candidate loop; prioritize proven hotspots with measurable wins.
asi.observations: Both quality and form ratios worsened in this run, with form degradation dominating.

description: Replace remove_people set-filter strategy with ordered two-pointer subtraction (matching combination order) to avoid per-candidate set work.

asi.hypothesis: Candidates from list.combinations preserve source order, so ordered subtraction should remove members faster than building/consulting sets.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary metric regressed (2.7888 -> 3.1393), so this removal strategy did not improve end-to-end performance.
asi.next_action_hint: Deprioritize remove_people micro-optimizations; focus on assignment/scoring work that dominates total runtime.
asi.observations: form_ratio worsened notably (~2.43), outweighing any small local gains.

description: Add quality-endpoint-only weights_override fast path (explicit alpha/beta/gamma/delta + normalize=false) to bypass resolve_weights while leaving form path unchanged.

asi.hypothesis: Applying direct Weights construction only in calculate_team_quality should retain quality-side gains without affecting form candidate scoring.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary metric regressed strongly (2.7888 -> 3.2905); this approach did not translate into benchmark improvement.
asi.next_action_hint: Pause weight-resolution refactors; focus on assignment/search internals where prior keeps came from.
asi.observations: Both quality and form worsened in this run, with form_ratio ~2.51 driving most regression.

description: Precompute compat delta weight once in form_teams and pass through recursive search to avoid per-candidate weight-dict lookup during adjusted quality calculation.

asi.hypothesis: Hoisting the compat delta coefficient out of candidate scoring should remove repeated dict lookups and reduce formation overhead.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary metric regressed significantly (2.7888 -> 3.2321), with much worse form ratio.
asi.next_action_hint: Drop this line of optimization; focus on larger structural wins in assignment/search rather than tiny coefficient lookups.
asi.observations: quality_ratio stayed near baseline but form_ratio climbed to ~2.59, overwhelming any micro-optimization benefit.

description: Key unique-assignment DP memo only by used task-bitmask (drop derived member-index from memo key) to reduce memo-key arithmetic and dict cardinality.

asi.hypothesis: In unique assignment DP, member_index is implied by recursion depth/used-mask, so memoing by used_mask alone should reduce lookup overhead.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary metric regressed (2.7888 -> 2.9074), so reduced memo key dimensionality did not improve end-to-end performance.
asi.next_action_hint: Investigate score-matrix construction and coverage loops directly; memo-key micro-optimization appears low leverage.
asi.observations: quality_ratio improved slightly but form_ratio worsened, leading to net combined regression.

description: Precompute per-task scoring metadata (task preference map + compat default) once at form_teams entry and reuse across recursive states.

asi.hypothesis: Task preference lookup/default derivation is invariant per task, so global precomputation should remove repeated per-state setup cost in formation search.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary metric regressed (2.7888 -> 3.1319), so this metadata plumbing did not improve benchmark performance.
asi.next_action_hint: Try reducing core scoring costs inside candidate evaluation rather than additional metadata indirection.
asi.observations: Both quality and form components moved worse in this run; extra dict/meta lookups likely outweighed saved setup work.

description: Use string.byte_size instead of string.length in non-empty string decoder checks to avoid grapheme-count overhead during JSON decode.

asi.hypothesis: Byte-size emptiness checks should be much cheaper than grapheme length checks and reduce decode overhead in quality/form JSON parsing.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary metric regressed (2.7888 -> 3.0024), so decode-side change did not improve combined objective.
asi.next_action_hint: Profile decode/validation deeper before further codec tweaks; this isolated change did not convert to runtime gains.
asi.observations: quality ratio worsened while form ratio improved slightly; overall metric still worse and stability CV high.

description: Build candidate teammate-id set once and reuse it for both remaining-people filtering and social-preference checks in formation candidate loop.

asi.hypothesis: Eliminating duplicate set construction per candidate should reduce formation-loop allocation/hash overhead.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary metric regressed (2.7888 -> 2.9536), so the shared-set refactor did not help overall performance.
asi.next_action_hint: Try reducing costly scoring calls per candidate rather than micro-allocation sharing in surrounding loop.
asi.observations: form ratio stayed close to prior range but quality ratio worsened, yielding a worse combined score.

description: In unique-assignment reconstruction, store task-skill IDs by index (String) instead of full TaskSkill records to reduce lookup payload size.

asi.hypothesis: Replacing task-index lookup values from TaskSkill records to plain IDs will lower dict/object overhead during assignment reconstruction.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary metric regressed strongly (2.7888 -> 3.1803), so this data-shape change is not beneficial.
asi.next_action_hint: Avoid reconstruction micro-tuning; focus on hot loops that run during DP scoring, not post-processing.
asi.observations: quality improved slightly but form ratio worsened significantly, causing overall loss.

description: Add exact branch-and-bound pruning in formation search using a safe per-task quality upper bound to skip candidates that cannot beat current best objective.

asi.hypothesis: Using a mathematically safe upper bound for remaining task quality should prune many recursive branches without changing optimal output.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary metric regressed (2.7888 -> 2.9397), so pruning overhead outweighed skipped work on this benchmark.
asi.next_action_hint: If revisiting, tighten upper bounds significantly (task-specific caps) or apply pruning only after a strong incumbent is found.
asi.observations: quality ratio improved sharply (~3.76), but form ratio worsened (~2.30) with high variance; net combined loss.

description: Add happy-path team-quality validation fast checks (duplicate/unknown flags) to avoid full duplicate/unknown list construction unless an error is detected.

asi.hypothesis: Validation on valid payloads can be accelerated by checking cheap boolean flags first and only materializing sorted error lists on failure paths.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary metric regressed heavily (2.7888 -> 3.2535), so added fast-path plumbing did not improve runtime.
asi.next_action_hint: Undo validation fast-path experiments and focus on algorithmic scoring/search changes that showed prior wins.
asi.observations: form ratio degraded substantially (~2.57), indicating extra validation logic overhead outweighed avoided list construction.

description: Drop sorting from people_signature memo key generation (retain original remaining-people order) to reduce per-state key-construction overhead.

asi.hypothesis: Remaining people order is already stable through filtering, so sorting IDs in memo signatures is redundant overhead.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary metric regressed (2.7888 -> 3.0755), so removing sort did not improve end-to-end benchmark.
asi.next_action_hint: Do not revisit unsorted signatures unless accompanied by a stronger state-representation redesign.
asi.observations: Both quality and form ratios worsened in this run; no evidence of memo-key win.

description: Add formation candidate-quality cache keyed by (task_id, candidate_people_signature) to reuse repeated team scoring across recursive states.

asi.hypothesis: The same candidate team for a task can be encountered across multiple recursive branches, so caching scored TeamResult should reduce repeated scoring work.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary metric regressed (2.7888 -> 2.8920), mainly from worse form ratio in this run.
asi.next_action_hint: If revisiting, optimize cache key construction (avoid signature strings) or enable cache only for deeper recursion levels where reuse is higher.
asi.observations: quality_ratio improved materially (~3.69), but form_ratio increased (~2.26), so cache overhead likely outweighed reuse with current string keys.

description: Reintroduce formation candidate-quality cache using compact bitmask candidate keys (task_id + people mask) to reduce string-signature overhead.

asi.hypothesis: Candidate-quality caching may help if key overhead is minimized; bitmask keys should be cheaper than string signatures.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary metric regressed (2.7888 -> 3.1055), so cached scoring still underperforms on benchmark workload.
asi.next_action_hint: Abandon cache-based approach for now; reuse appears too low relative to cache machinery cost.
asi.observations: form ratio remained high (~2.39) and overall runtime worsened despite compact keys.

description: Switch formation memo keys from string signatures to compact integer state keys (remaining task count + people bitmask).

asi.hypothesis: Replacing expensive string signature construction/hashing with integer keys should accelerate recursive memo lookups in form search.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary metric regressed substantially (2.7888 -> 3.2484), so integer-state memo keys did not improve this workload.
asi.next_action_hint: Stop memo-key representation experiments; prioritize reducing scoring cost per candidate or revisit benchmark variance control.
asi.observations: form ratio worsened strongly (~2.47), indicating key-construction savings were outweighed by new bitmask bookkeeping.

description: Add Compat equal-partition greedy assignment fast path (single-skill-per-member selection with deterministic fallback) to bypass unique DP in hot paths.

asi.hypothesis: Replacing compat equal-size assignment DP with linear greedy matching should cut scoring cost for common quality/form workloads.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary metric regressed (2.7888 -> 3.1415), so this greedy fast path is slower in practice on benchmark workloads.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep DP path; explore lower-level DP optimizations or other scoring components instead of algorithm replacement.
asi.observations: Parity checks passed, but both quality and form ratios worsened enough to make this a clear regression.

description: No-code-change rerun to quantify current benchmark variance before next optimization slice.

asi.hypothesis: Re-running unchanged best code estimates noise floor and prevents over-attributing tiny metric shifts to code edits.
asi.rollback_reason: Discarded because this run has no implementation change and metric drifted upward significantly.
asi.next_action_hint: Treat sub-~0.1 combined-ratio changes as noise unless reproduced; prioritize bigger algorithmic wins.
asi.observations: Unchanged code moved from 2.79 best to 3.18 here, confirming large variance in current form-heavy benchmark.

description: Add formation-level caches for team personality/social components and feed them into scoring via component-override API to avoid recomputation across candidate evaluations.

asi.hypothesis: Caching team-intrinsic components (personality/social) by team signature will reduce repeated work in form search where many candidate teams recur.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary metric regressed (2.7888 -> 2.9235); cache keying/lookup overhead outweighed saved component computation on this benchmark.
asi.next_action_hint: If revisiting, switch to cheaper team-signature keys (bitmasks) and cache only high-reuse depths to reduce overhead.
asi.observations: quality_ratio improved notably (~3.83), but form_ratio remained high (~2.23) with large variance, yielding net regression.

description: Add exact-search masked fast path for uncapped formation (precompute all task candidates + recurse on remaining people bitmask) to avoid repeated combinations/remove_people work.

asi.hypothesis: For uncapped exact search, precomputing candidate combinations and using bitmask state transitions should reduce repeated list.combinations and filtering overhead.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary metric regressed (2.7888 -> 3.0648), so masked fast path did not improve end-to-end performance.
asi.next_action_hint: Abandon this large state-representation change for now; pursue targeted hot-path wins with lower overhead and better locality.
asi.observations: quality_ratio improved slightly but form_ratio worsened notably, likely due extra mask/key bookkeeping and broader candidate iteration overhead.

description: Add Compat small-team (n<=3) exact permutation fast path in unique assignment to bypass DP memo/dict overhead for tiny equal partitions.

asi.hypothesis: For very small equal partitions common in form workloads, direct permutation evaluation should outperform generic DP/memo bookkeeping.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary metric regressed significantly (2.7888 -> 3.3581), indicating the permutation fast path is slower in practice.
asi.next_action_hint: Drop small-team permutation rewrites and continue targeting broader hot paths with proven wins.
asi.observations: Both quality and form ratios worsened, with especially poor quality variance; no evidence this approach helps.

description: Use request-level explicit delta weight directly when available to avoid per-candidate quality-weights dict lookup during compat social adjustment.

asi.hypothesis: When request.delta is set, skipping dict_get on returned weights should shave overhead in formation candidate scoring.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary metric regressed sharply (2.7888 -> 3.5067), so this micro-optimization is not viable.
asi.next_action_hint: Avoid further delta-lookup micro-tweaks; focus on higher-leverage algorithmic changes with measurable upside.
asi.observations: Both quality and form ratios degraded substantially in this run.

description: Replace candidate social-preference detection set-building with pairwise teammate preference checks to avoid per-candidate set allocation.

asi.hypothesis: For small team sizes, pairwise preference checks should be cheaper than building teammate-id sets and scanning with set membership.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary metric regressed (2.7888 -> 3.1335), so pairwise social detection did not help runtime.
asi.next_action_hint: Stop iterating on social-preference detection micro-optimizations; focus on larger algorithmic bottlenecks.
asi.observations: form_ratio worsened significantly (~2.48) and quality variance spiked; net result clearly worse.

description: Enable compat direct-coverage matrix fast path only for TeamQualityRequest endpoint (keep formation path on generic coverage) via assign_task_skills options plumbing.

asi.hypothesis: Quality-only activation of compat matrix specialization should capture quality gains without impacting formation runtime.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary metric regressed heavily (2.7888 -> 3.3368), so selective quality-path specialization did not help combined benchmark.
asi.next_action_hint: Drop compat-matrix specialization experiments; investigate entirely different hotspots instead of further routing/plumbing variants.
asi.observations: Both quality and form ratios worsened in this run despite limiting the optimization to quality request path.

description: Add specialized 3-person branch in team_personality_score (direct stddev/max computations) to reduce allocations/folds in common team-size-3 form scoring.

asi.hypothesis: Since benchmark form tasks commonly use team size 3, an unrolled 3-person personality path should reduce per-candidate scoring overhead.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary metric regressed strongly (2.7888 -> 3.3605), so this specialization is not beneficial in aggregate.
asi.next_action_hint: Avoid further micro-specialization in personality scoring; seek larger wins in formation search structure or decoding path.
